steps.why: An English question needs an auxiliary (do / does / did / am / is / are / have) before the subject.

steps.title: Question forms
steps.html:
Question wordAuxiliarySubjectRest
—Doyoulive near here?
Wheredoyoulive?
Whatdoyoudo?
Whatdidyoudo at the weekend?
How longhaveyouworked there?
—Areyoubusy today?

Word order is fixed: (question word) + auxiliary + subject + verb.

Present Simple uses do / does; Past Simple uses did. After did the verb goes back to its base form: What did you do?, not What did you did?

Be needs no extra auxiliary — it moves in front of the subject itself: Are you busy?

The most common mistake is keeping statement order: Where you live? is wrong.

How long have you …? is the Present Perfect. It comes back properly in Unit 6 and Unit 12.

steps.title: Three lives, one set of questions
steps.sub: Three people, one set of questions.
steps.html:
From a weekly blog

Every Monday I post three short interviews on my blog. I ask everybody the same questions, and the answers are never the same.

Dilnaz, 27, Almaty. Where do you live? “In a flat near the park, with my sister.” What do you do? “I’m a psychologist. I work with children.” How long have you had this job? “For four years. I still love it.” What did you do at the weekend? “Nothing special. I had a long chat with my sister and we watched an old film. My week is busy from Monday to Friday, so at the weekend I do very little.”

Marat, 41, Karaganda. Where do you live? “In a small house outside the city.” What do you do? “I’m a reviewer. I write about books for a magazine.” Do you enjoy it? “Most of the time. I read four books a month, so I keep a record of everything I read.” What did you do at the weekend? “I made a promise to my daughter, so we spent the whole of Saturday in the mountains.”

Aisha, 34, Astana. Where do you live? “With my husband and his parents.” How often do you see your relatives? “Every day! We have a good relationship, but we are eleven people in one house.” What do you do at the weekend? “I text my friends, I post photos, and I sleep. That is my dream weekend.”

Three lives, one set of questions. Ask them yourself — you will hear something you did not expect.

The violet lines are the questions the writer asks. Look at the word order in each one.
